issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/msdn-magazine/2013/march/async-await-best-practices-in-asynchronous-programming (cited as "Stephen Cleary: Async/Await best practices" for async void and .Result/deadlock behaviour)
issues.problem: The fetch status is unknown, with no title, no excerpt and no fetch date. The page cannot be confirmed to exist or to support the claims it is cited for: that async void is meant for event handlers, that .Result or .Wait() can deadlock under a single-threaded SynchronizationContext, and that .Result wraps exceptions in AggregateException. The generator notes also say the archive URL path still has to be checked.
issues.suggestedFix: Re-fetch and confirm that the page exists and covers async void and the .Result deadlock. If it cannot be confirmed, replace it with a source that was actually fetched, for example the original unit-testing-best-practices page if it covers async tests, or the xUnit or NUnit documentation on async tests. Another option is to rely only on the async-return-types page, whose excerpt supports the async void claims.

issues.claim: The framework has nothing to await, so some frameworks refuse to run such tests and in others the result is unreliable.
issues.problem: The claim is vague and partly inaccurate. NUnit rejects async void tests, and xUnit v3 fails them, but xUnit v2 does wait for them through a custom SynchronizationContext. The statement that the framework has nothing to await is true, but the "unreliable" part is not accurate for every framework. The RU text has the same wording.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword in both locales to say that frameworks cannot reliably await or observe the exception of an async void test. Depending on the framework and version, such a test is rejected, or it may pass before its body completes or miss exceptions. Optionally name NUnit as one framework that rejects it.

issues.problem: The English term "deadlock" is left untranslated in the middle of a Russian sentence. This is unnatural, although the meaning is clear.
issues.suggestedFix: Write "это может привести к взаимной блокировке (deadlock)" in both the explanation and optionExplanations.c.

issues.claim: Libraries such as Moq and NSubstitute call their objects mocks, but the same object is often used as a stub
issues.problem: NSubstitute calls its objects "substitutes", not mocks. Moq does use Mock<T>. The wording is slightly inaccurate. The RU text has the same problem.
issues.suggestedFix: Write "Libraries such as Moq and NSubstitute are called mocking libraries, but the objects they create are often used as stubs". In Russian: "Библиотеки вроде Moq и NSubstitute называют библиотеками для мокирования, но создаваемые ими объекты часто служат заглушками".
